from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
from typing import Any

import pytest

from llm_router._internal.runtime.router import RouterRuntime
from llm_router._internal.runtime import router as router_module
import tests.llm_router.support.workers.timeout

pytestmark = pytest.mark.verification_kind("unit")

ResolvedRequest = getattr(router_module, "ResolvedRequest", object)
LLMRouterResponse = getattr(router_module, "LLMRouterResponse", object)


class BlockingSyncExecutor:
    """Sync executor that blocks the first route attempt on an event."""

    def __init__(self, block_event: Any, fallback_response: Any) -> None:
        self.block_event = block_event
        self.fallback_response = fallback_response
        self.attempts: list[Any] = []
        self.first_route_completed = False

    def execute(self, request: Any) -> Any:
        self.attempts.append(request)
        if len(self.attempts) == 1:
            self.block_event.wait(timeout=1.5)
            self.first_route_completed = True
            return self.fallback_response
        return self.fallback_response


@pytest.mark.verifies("REQ_ROUTE_TIMEOUT_FALLBACK[revision==1]")
def test_sync_timeout_stops_waiting_and_falls_back() -> None:
    threading = getattr(dataclasses, "sys").modules["threading"]
    time = getattr(dataclasses, "sys").modules["time"]

    block_event = threading.Event()
    expected_response = object.__new__(LLMRouterResponse)
    executor = BlockingSyncExecutor(
        block_event=block_event,
        fallback_response=expected_response,
    )

    runtime = object.__new__(RouterRuntime)
    runtime._executor = executor

    req_primary = object.__new__(ResolvedRequest)
    req_fallback = object.__new__(ResolvedRequest)

    start_time = time.monotonic()

    # Route 1: times out within 0.02s
    with pytest.raises(TimeoutError, match="Attempt timed out"):
        runtime._call_sync_with_timeout(req_primary, timeout_seconds=0.02)

    elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time

    # Under the original code, pool.shutdown(wait=False) returns immediately.
    # Under the defect, pool.shutdown(wait=True) blocks until the worker completes.
    assert not executor.first_route_completed
    assert not block_event.is_set()
    assert elapsed < 0.5

    # Fallback to route 2 continues and succeeds before route 1 finishes
    fallback_response = runtime._call_sync_with_timeout(
        req_fallback,
        timeout_seconds=0.02,
    )
    assert fallback_response is expected_response
    assert not executor.first_route_completed

    # Release the first route worker to allow clean thread exit
    block_event.set()
